benchmark: Street Vision Pipeline — Per-Image Inference Latency
description: Per-image SegFormer-B2 inference latency on a 4-core CPU, end-to-end through the demo-mode pipeline (HTTP fetch + model forward + post-processing). The benchmark script attempted four batch sizes (10, 50, 100, 500) but the demo-mode batch cap of 20 means the 50/100/500 attempts all collapsed to an effective batch of 20. We therefore report per-image latency as the headline metric — it is the only quantity the data actually supports. A real scaling study would require lifting the cap (a one-line change in backend/config.py) and re-running.

configuration.data_source: demo-mode synthetic pipeline (no live Street View calls)

raw_runs.notes: Below the cap; ran exactly as requested.

supports_claims: Per-image SegFormer-B2 latency on 4-core CPU is ~0.30 s, stable to ±0.0001 s across four independent runs.
End-to-end throughput including HTTP and post-processing is ~3.32 images/s.
Per-image latency is independent of effective batch size in the 10-20 image range tested.
does_not_support_claims: Scaling behaviour above batch size 20 — three of the four runs collapsed to the same effective batch of 20, so we have no data on how throughput changes at larger batches.
GPU performance — all measurements are CPU-only.
Latency on real Street View images — runs used demo-mode synthetic pipeline.
